_README: TRANCHE 10 - PATCH. Article defect + raw blanks inside choose_one options, both pylon bodies.
1. ARTICLE - same defect as audit_right, same fix. 'to install a {{dimensions}}' is only
correct for values starting with a consonant sound. "a 4' x 8'" but "an 8' x 4'".
Dimensions are a landlord-supplied fill, so this is not hypothetical. Article promoted to
its own choose_one {a, an} immediately before the dimensions token, first position only.
sign_pn_choose_2 appears TWICE in panel_new_pylon and is untouched - both occurrences take
the same value ('monument' or 'pylon'), same reasoning as audit_blank_1.
2. RAW BLANK INSIDE A CHOOSE_ONE OPTION - your scan found it, and the fix needs your ruling.
sign_pe_choose_1 and sign_pn_choose_1 both offer '__________ position from the top' as an
option. That blank emits verbatim when the option is chosen.
I have keyed it as a NESTED TOKEN inside the option value:
['top position', '{{param:sign_pe_position_ordinal}} position from the top']
This follows directly from what your scan established: option values emit exactly as body
text does. If they emit like body text, they should be substitutable like body text.
BUT I do not know whether your loader/emitter substitutes inside option values, and I am
not assuming it. If it does not, the alternatives are:
(a) make substitution-in-options a supported feature (my preference - it generalises,
and any future option carrying a value has the same need);
(b) split choose_1 into a two-rung structure where the ordinal is a sibling fill that
only resolves when the second option is selected - more machinery, and the gating
lives at position level which is the wrong granularity;
(c) drop the option to a plain fill carrying the whole phrase - loses the closed domain
and lets a dealmaker type anything into a slot with two legal shapes.
Tell me which and I re-key. Do not load this tranche until that is settled - the nested
token is the only part of it that assumes something about your schema.
3. NOT FIXED, NEEDS YOUR FIXTURE - a space before a period.
Both bodies read '...located at {{param:...blank}} .' with a space between the token and
the full stop. Filled, that emits 'located at Powder Springs Road .' which is visibly
wrong. It appears IDENTICALLY in both bodies, which says it came from the template rather
than being a transcription slip.
I have deliberately NOT removed it. If the sent Powder Springs LOI carries that space,
removing it fails the acceptance-test byte diff, and the fixture is the authority - not my
sense of what looks right. Check the fixture and tell me: if the space is absent there,
I will send tranche 11 removing it from both bodies; if present, it stays and gets an
extraction_note so nobody 'fixes' it later.
4. THREE MORE DEFECTS FROM YOUR SCAN, NOT IN THIS TRANCHE - send me the full current values
and I will patch them:
initial_cotenancy_optional_2 - raw blank AND an unbalanced instruction bracket
('[IDENTIFY KEY TENANT(S)' with no closing ']')
utilities_optional_1         - '$____________'
eu_remedy                    - '___ percent (__%)' - TWO blanks, and by the audit_right
precedent almost certainly one value used twice
I have fragments, not full values. Reconstructing a param value from a fragment is how the
wrong thing gets patched confidently.
5. YOUR SCAN-SCOPE CORRECTION IS THE REAL FINDING. 'Scan the bodies' meaning 'scan body_text'
because that is where the first instance happened to live is the same failure as
LIKE '%_%' - a rule that cannot fail on input it never looks at. Worth stating as a rule:
when a scan finds a defect class, establish every surface that class can occupy BEFORE
declaring the scan clean. Three of the five defects lived somewhere the scan wasn't looking.
